correctness.rationale: For the exact stationary linearized system, the position autocorrelation is the first diagonal entry of the matrix exponential. In the overdamped case the ratio to the variance-matched first-order autocorrelation reduces to a scalar function whose derivative changes sign exactly once and whose limit is negative, yielding one positive crossover. The repeated-root case has a one-turning-point log ratio. In the underdamped case odd half-period lags make the second-order correlation exactly negative while the first-order correlation is positive. The proof states all parameter ranges and does not extrapolate from simulation.

value.rationale: Sampling lag is intrinsic to empirical autocorrelation-based early-warning signals. The theorem replaces an unrestricted recent dominance claim by a sharp regime-aware statement: one crossover in the nonoscillatory case and exact negative bands in the oscillatory case. This identifies when inertia enhances versus suppresses the same variance-matched indicator and is directly useful for interpreting discretely sampled tipping diagnostics.
